1. The National Historical Museum, the Afro Brazil Museum and the National Ethology Museum are monumental museums in the Lusophones.
the Lusophone monumental museum is a site of negotiation and struggle over ideas of Africa and Nation, and the way in which these are represented in the museum space.

the three case study museums have different ideas about what Africa is and how to use it in exhibitions, and that these ideas are connected to their own specific national identity discursive strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the monumental museums in question mobilise the ideas of Africa and Nation, in order to produce and represent identity discourses.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the monumental museums of the Lusophone countries have been and continue to be important sites for the creation and mobilisation of national identity discourses, and that these discourses are not static but rather are constantly changing in response to the political, social, economic and cultural contexts in which the museums operate.
the three museums are monumental in the way they are part of the social arena, and that they are also part of a hegemonic process of nation building.
the monumental museums in the Lusophonic world, as institutions, are still very much concerned with the production of national identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are interested in how the Lusophone museums are monumental and what they do to the nation. In order to do so we are going to examine how the three museums we selected employ the ideas of nation and Africa in their long term exhibition.
we are not only interested in the ways in which the museums are representing 'Africa' and the 'Nation' but also in how these representations are being produced and consumed.

this thesis is an attempt to understand how these three museums are monumental and how their exhibitions employ ideas of 'Africa' and nation in the 21 st century, while at the same time reflecting on the consequences and possibilities of their discursive productions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the museums are in a process of change, which is a result of the social demands of the 21st Century.
museums are not just passive reflectors of the social arena, but also active agents in its production.

there are diverse and multiple forms of monumentality, which are the consequence of struggles for representation and for participation in the social sphere, here understood as a hegemony and counter-hegemony.
